source.title: PIM-QAT: Neural Network Quantization for Processing-In-Memory (PIM) Systems
source.authors: Qing Jin; Zhiyu Chen; Jian Ren; Yan-Yu Li; Yanzhi Wang; Kai-Min Yang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some figure and table text is garbled in the supplied extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and evaluates PIM-aware training as a method for improving inference on PIM hardware. It does not measure the training classification error named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports inference accuracy, not training classification error. Its explicit statement that some unscaled PIM-QAT training does not converge is recorded as a related finding under fits_no_version; cited results and inference-accuracy comparisons are not rows.
record.test_reason: Figure A5 reports training classification-error curves for ResNet20 on CIFAR-10 under 4-bit and 5-bit PIM quantization, bearing on V1 in a new quantized-training setting. The record overlooks these curves. Their values are unreadable in the supplied text, so a near-zero training-error verdict cannot be established.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: PIM-aware training incorporates the extra hardware quantization; forward and backward rescaling address training instability; BN calibration and adjusted training precision improve inference robustness to hardware non-idealities. Failure of conventionally trained baseline models on PIM hardware is an inference failure, not evidence that their original training failed.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains quantized networks for PIM inference and evaluates inference accuracy; it does not test the claim's training-error outcomes or recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Training convergence depends on PIM decomposition scheme, PIM bit-width and whether forward or backward rescaling is applied. Inference accuracy also varies with PIM resolution, noise, decomposition scheme and BN calibration.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.3 reports non-convergence in some low-precision PIM settings without backward rescaling and says rescaling restores convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PIM quantization can destabilize training, and rescaling can restore convergence in some decomposition and precision settings.

record.problems: The convergence statement is qualitative and does not give training-error values or uncertainty. Several accuracy findings are presented in figures whose extracted text is garbled; those inference results do not measure the claim's training-error outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: Inference-accuracy results in Tables 3, 4, A2, A3 and A4 and Figures 4–6 were left out because they do not measure training classification error. Cited prior-work findings were also excluded.

untested.parts: Random or corrupted labels; model-size comparisons; effects of early stopping and regularization. Figure A5 covers only clean-label ResNet20 training under particular PIM quantization and rescaling conditions.
Teacher-student spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation across depth and matched plain-versus-residual comparisons.
Comparative initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth. The statement that He initialization is ineffective here does not supply these comparisons.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature trajectories, catapult recovery and edge-of-stability behavior.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup. BN calibration concerns inference statistics.

missing.what: Training classification-error trajectories in Figure A5 for ResNet20 on CIFAR-10, at 4-bit and 5-bit PIM precision, comparing vanilla, backward rescaling, forward rescaling and both. Extract final training errors and whether they approach zero; the supplied figure text does not permit reading these values. These training results are neither recorded nor declared in rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is assigned because R1 does not measure a listed version's outcome and Figure A5's training-error values are unreadable. Tables reporting validation or inference accuracy cannot substitute for training error.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, including corrupted or random labels; effects of model size, early stopping and regularization.
Teacher-student local minima and the effect of student width.
Plain versus residual network training error across depth; shortcut and normalization comparisons.
Comparative initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Training behavior above or near a learning-rate stability threshold.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, including comparison with Fixup.

rows.subject: neural network composed of repeated blocks
rows.operation_detail: PIM-QAT without the proposed backward scaling, using conventional STE scaling
rows.note: The paper states that proper initialization as proposed in He et al. (2015) is not effective in this case; it does not report training classification error.
rows.check: Qualitative non-convergence does not establish the training classification error named by V1. The repeated-block architecture belongs to Theorem 2; the experimental architecture is unspecified in this passage. The 7-bit example also needs qualification: Table A3 reports 88.8% validation accuracy without rescaling at 7 bits, so failure is not universal at that precision.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
